criteria.criterion: A docker compose recreate of review-bot cannot leave a container that has closed its listener but not exited: shutdown either completes within the stop timeout or the process is forced down, so the port is released for the replacement.
In-flight review tasks are cancelled (or awaited under a bounded deadline) during lifespan shutdown rather than blocking it indefinitely.
The reconcile loop is not stopped while the process continues serving/working — or, if shutdown has begun, the process reliably terminates so a fresh container restores both intake paths.

A health/liveness signal distinguishes 'listener closed, process alive' from healthy, so this state alarms instead of presenting as a silent 502. Done: the compose healthcheck (infra/compose/docker-compose.yml) probes the process's OWN listener at /health on 127.0.0.1
Regression test: a SIGTERM delivered while a long review is in flight results in process exit (not an indefinitely-hung shutdown) within the compose stop timeout.
Bug 'Autodeploy recreate leaves review-bot a zombie' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces.

findings.criterion: A health/liveness signal distinguishes "listener closed, process alive" from healthy, so this state alarms instead of presenting as a silent 502. Done: the compose healthcheck (infra/compose/docker-compose.yml) probes the process's OWN listener at /health on 127.0.0.1
findings.detail: The review-bot service in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml (lines 74–276) has no `healthcheck:` stanza. Only the `mcp` service (line 507) has a healthcheck. Dockerfile.reviewbot also has no HEALTHCHECK instruction. The AC claims the compose healthcheck probes the process's own listener at /health on 127.0.0.1 so the zombie state is detected as unhealthy, but no such healthcheck exists for the review-bot service in the codebase.
findings.title: review-bot healthcheck missing from docker-compose.yml and Dockerfile.reviewbot

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
